_about: Curated year-by-year supplement written for GeoHistory from general knowledge (conservative: well-established dates only). Each entry names the English Wikipedia article it is about; tools/build_curated.py sets "verified" when the Wikidata item of that article carries the same year. Places are approximate (nearest town).

events.label: Indonesia proclaims independence
events.desc: Sukarno and Hatta declare independence from the Netherlands, which recognises it in 1949.

events.label: Vietnam declares independence
events.desc: Ho Chi Minh reads the declaration in Hanoi.

events.label: Philippines becomes independent
events.desc: The United States recognises Philippine independence.

events.label: India and Pakistan become independent
events.desc: British India is divided into two dominions.

events.label: Ceylon becomes independent
events.desc: Ceylon, later Sri Lanka, becomes a dominion.

events.label: Israel declares independence
events.desc: The British mandate ends and the first Arab–Israeli war begins.

events.label: Netherlands recognises Indonesian independence
events.desc: Sovereignty is transferred after four years of fighting and negotiation.

events.label: Fall of Dien Bien Phu
events.desc: The Viet Minh defeat the French garrison.

events.label: Geneva Accords
events.desc: French rule in Indochina ends; Vietnam is divided at the 17th parallel.

events.label: Algerian War begins
events.desc: The FLN launches attacks across Algeria.

events.label: Bandung Conference
events.desc: Twenty-nine Asian and African states meet in Indonesia.

events.label: Tunisia becomes independent
events.desc: France recognises Tunisian independence, weeks after Morocco's.

events.label: Suez Crisis
events.desc: Israel, Britain and France attack Egypt after the canal is nationalised, and withdraw under pressure.

events.label: Ghana becomes independent
events.desc: The Gold Coast is the first sub-Saharan colony to gain independence.

events.label: Malaya becomes independent
events.desc: The Federation of Malaya leaves British rule.

events.label: Belgian Congo becomes independent
events.desc: Independence is followed within days by mutiny and the Congo Crisis.

events.label: Nigeria becomes independent
events.desc: One of seventeen African states to become independent in 1960.

events.label: Tanganyika becomes independent
events.desc: It unites with Zanzibar as Tanzania in 1964.

events.label: Algeria becomes independent
events.desc: Independence follows the Évian Accords and a referendum.

events.label: Kenya becomes independent
events.desc: Jomo Kenyatta is the first prime minister.

events.label: Rhodesia declares independence unilaterally
events.desc: The white-minority government breaks with Britain.

events.label: Bangladesh wins independence
events.desc: Pakistani forces in the east surrender to Indian and Bangladeshi forces.

events.label: Carnation Revolution
events.desc: A coup in Lisbon ends the dictatorship and opens the way to independence for Portugal's colonies.

events.label: Mozambique becomes independent
events.desc: Independence from Portugal.

events.label: Angola becomes independent
events.desc: Independence from Portugal as civil war begins.

events.label: Zimbabwe becomes independent
events.desc: Majority rule after the Lancaster House Agreement.
